summary: Today’s pulse tracks Fall in official Ebola numbers appears to be good news but it's not that simple, Ukraine strikes cargo ships and admits Romania drone blast, and Senate Republicans pass bill authorizing $70bn for immigration enforcement in vote-a-rama – US politics live. Across BBC and Guardian, the strongest repeated signals are yeast, murder, and people. In the background, How did the notion of ‘two-tier policing’ evolve, and does it really exist and Former student charged after crossbow shooting at Surrey University keep the wider picture in motion.

headlines.title: Fall in official Ebola numbers appears to be good news but it's not that simple
headlines.description: There are now 380 confirmed cases of Ebola in DR Congo, far lower than initial estimates of suspected cases, writes Fergus Walsh.

headlines.title: Ukraine strikes cargo ships and admits Romania drone blast
headlines.description: Ukraine says it struck five ships carrying illegal cargo in the Sea of Azov and in coastal waters of Russian-occupied territories.

headlines.title: Senate Republicans pass bill authorizing $70bn for immigration enforcement in vote-a-rama – US politics live
headlines.description: Republican senator Lindsey Graham said he was ‘very proud of my Republican colleagues for… making sure that Border Patrol and ICE are fully funded’ US district judge John McConnell in Providence, Rhode Island, has ruled that the US Citizenship and Immigration Services had adopted a series of unlawful policies targeting people from 39 African, Asian, Latin American and Middle Eastern countries. With a great Jobs Report, like just announced, stocks should go up, not down. That’s the way it was for 200 years. Growth does not mean inflation! How else can a Country attain GREATNESS???

headlines.title: How did the notion of ‘two-tier policing’ evolve, and does it really exist?
headlines.description: Data discredits claims reawakened by the death of Henry Nowak that UK police actions disadvantage white people The US government has joined criticism of alleged two-tier policing in the UK in the wake of Henry Nowak’s murder . How did the term enter the mainstream, and is there any basis for the claim?

headlines.title: Former student charged after crossbow shooting at Surrey University
headlines.description: Almunthir Daqamah, 21, charged with attempted murder as campus safety officer said to be in stable condition A man accused of attempted murder after a member of staff at the University of Surrey was shot with a crossbow in Guildford has appeared in court. Almunthir Daqamah, 21, is alleged to have shot Robert Tytler, a campus safety officer, after he told the former student to leave a student village on Thursday morning.

headlines.title: Scientists make sourdough bread using yeast found in 5,000-year-old mummy
headlines.description: Team now plans to see if they can use yeast strains harvested from Ötzi the Iceman to brew beer too Scientists have baked a sourdough loaf of bread using yeast strains harvested from a 5,000-year-old mummy and now plan to see if they can use them to brew beer too. The yeast came from Ötzi the Iceman, a famous corpse remarkably preserved by being frozen in Alpine ice near the Italy-Austria border until he was discovered in 1991. Ötzi has been the subject of intense study since he was found and has shed much light on pre-historic European people and their way of life.

headlinePool.title: EU must prove it is capable and willing to take in new members, leaders say
headlinePool.description: Von der Leyen tells Balkans summit that bloc needs to make enlargement process ‘faster and more credible’ The EU must prove its willingness and ability to take in new members and speed up its enlargement process, leaders of the bloc have said, as they gathered with their counterparts from six western Balkan countries that hope to join soon. “The European Union has to show that it is capable of enlarging and willing to enlarge, and we want to discuss that here,” Germany’s chancellor, Friedrich Merz, told reporters on Friday at the summit in Tivat, a coastal town in Montenegro.

headlinePool.title: Downing Street rejects US claim of ‘two-tiered policing’ over Henry Nowak death - UK politics live
headlinePool.description: PM’s spokesperson also dismissed remarks from Kemi Badenoch, who suggested the identity politics could lead to civil war A former chair of an influential parliamentary committee said it was “shocking” that the public spending watchdog had not established Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor’s income from subletting properties. Margaret Hodge, who led the public accounts committee, told BBC Radio 4’s Today programme she was “very concerned” that the National Audit Office (NAO) was not able to find out how much money the former prince had made from letting properties.

headlinePool.title: Australian housing was already cooling before the budget – but how cold it gets depends on two key factors
headlinePool.description: Most economists believe the chronic undersupply of homes will eventually push prices higher once interest rates ease and the tax changes are priced in In the three weeks after the negative gearing and capital gains tax changes were revealed in the 12 May budget, housing data has begun to show how they may affect Australia’s property market. Here’s what the data shows, and what could happen next.

headlinePool.title: South Africa rolls out game-changing HIV shot amid funding shortfalls
headlinePool.description: A new twice-yearly HIV prevention injection could transform South Africa's fight against the epidemic — but U.S. aid cuts and limited doses threaten to slow its impact.

headlinePool.title: Not the next R8? Audi reveals mid-engined plug-in hybrid V8 Nuvolari.
headlinePool.description: The Huracan gave us the R8s, now the Temerario lends itself to a new Audi.

headlinePool.title: International Space Station astronauts under evacuation orders over air leak
headlinePool.description: Nasa says Russian crew trying to fix worsening air leak in its portion of orbital laboratory International Space Station air leak: latest updates Astronauts onboard the International Space Station have been ordered to shelter in their spacecraft and prepare for potential evacuation as a Russian crew attempts to fix a worsening leak of air in its portion of the orbital laboratory, Nasa has said. The four astronauts of Nasa’s Crew-12 mission on the station – two US astronauts, a French astronaut and a Russian cosmonaut – received orders from Nasa mission control at 9.04am ET (2pm BST) on Friday to enter their Crew Dragon spacecraft docked to the station and don their spacesuits in case the air leak warranted an emergency evacuation, a Nasa official said.

headlinePool.title: California governor’s race remains too close to call as vote-counting continues
headlinePool.description: Experts warn primary vote-counting could go on for days in governor’s race, LA mayoral race and congressional races Three days after Californians headed to the polls, key races in the primary election remained too close to call and experts warned the counting could continue for days. In the governor’s race, the British-born conservative pundit Steve Hilton was narrowly leading with an estimated 60% of ballots counted by Friday morning. Xavier Becerra, a former US health and human services secretary under Joe Biden, followed closely behind, and billionaire Tom Steyer trailed behind the pair. The top two vote-getters will advance to the general election in November.
